newsitem.title: UK: Daily Mail to buy U.S. Dolphin Software.
newsitem.headline: Daily Mail to buy U.S. Dolphin Software.

text.p: Britain's Daily Mail and General Trust Plc (DMGT) said on Wednesday that it has invested $3.0 million for an initial 30 percent stake in U.S.-based Dolphin Software Inc. and plans to buy another 65 percent.
It said in a statement that the deal provides for Dolphin to become a 95 percent owned subsidiary by the year 2002. The payment will be based on the performance of the company.
DMGT, which publishes the national daily newspaper The Daily Mail, said the acquisition would expand the U.S. information publishing interests of its Harmsworth Publishing division.

Dolphin is based in Portland, Oregon and supplies information on the use, storage and transport of hazardous chemicals in electronic form, and provides related services required by U.S. regulations to users of such chemicals.
Dophin had net assets of 700,000 dollars on September 30, 1996.
DMGT also has the right to buy the final five percent of Dolphin from Mark Wysong, the managing director, if he leaves Dolphin's employment.
